input: Fix the dripping kitchen tap finally

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A dripping tap could mean replacing a washer, a cartridge, a ceramic disc, or the entire tap — the fix differs completely depending on the tap type and root cause.
Whether the user plans to DIY or hire a plumber changes every step of the plan — tools needed, skills required, and how to structure the task.
The tap type (mixer, pillar, monobloc, etc.) and whether it is hot, cold, or both sides dripping determines which parts and technique are needed.
A budget cap affects whether to repair vs. replace, and whether to buy premium parts or basic ones.
Access to tools (adjustable spanner, screwdrivers, etc.) and whether the water stopcock is known and accessible affects how quickly work can begin.
How urgently this needs fixing affects prioritisation — a heavy drip wasting significant water is more urgent than a slow drip.
The user's definition of done — simply stopping the drip vs. also upgrading the tap aesthetically — shapes the scope of work recommended.

gold.taskTitle: Fix the dripping kitchen tap finally
gold.taskDescription: Diagnose and repair a dripping kitchen tap to stop the leak permanently.

questions.title: What type of tap is it — mixer, pillar, or monobloc?
questions.description: Identifying the tap type determines which internal mechanism is involved (washer, cartridge, ceramic disc) and which repair approach applies.

questions.title: Are you planning to fix it yourself or hire a plumber?
questions.description: This determines whether the plan should be a step-by-step DIY guide with tool lists, or a checklist for briefing and managing a tradesperson.

questions.title: Do you know what is causing the drip — worn washer, faulty cartridge, something else?
questions.description: Understanding whether the fault has already been diagnosed narrows the scope of parts to source and steps to follow.

questions.title: How severe is the drip — a slow trickle or a steady stream?
questions.description: Severity affects urgency and whether a temporary fix is needed while awaiting parts or a plumber.

questions.title: What is your budget — repair with basic parts, or replace the tap entirely?
questions.description: Budget determines whether to source a cheap replacement washer, buy a quality cartridge kit, or invest in a full tap replacement.

questions.title: Do you have basic plumbing tools and know where the stopcock is?
questions.description: Tool availability and stopcock access are the two most common blockers that stall DIY tap repairs before they start.

questions.title: Is the goal just to stop the drip, or also to upgrade the tap?
questions.description: If the user wants to modernise the tap at the same time, the plan expands to include selection, purchase, and full installation of a new tap.
